issues.legal_issue: A consent order for eviction under rent-control legislation is not void merely because the tribunal made no express finding on the statutory ground, if the ground existed and the tribunal’s satisfaction can be inferred from the material or the tenant’s admission.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the statutory ground that he bona fide required the residential premises for his own occupation.
Before the parties reached a compromise, the landlord had testified about his need for the premises and filed documentary evidence supporting that claim; the tenant did not cross-examine him.
The tenant then unconditionally withdrew his defences and submitted to an eviction decree.
The tribunal recorded the compromise and ordered eviction by consent.
issues.conclusion: The eviction decree was not void or inexecutable. The tribunal’s satisfaction could be inferred from the evidence before it and the tenant’s unconditional withdrawal of defences, without a separate express finding or further enquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(1) and section 10(3)(a)(i), read with the bona fide-claim requirement in section 10, a landlord may obtain possession only on a statutory ground, and the tribunal must be satisfied that the ground exists. That satisfaction need not appear as an express judicial finding: it may be inferred where the tribunal had sufficient material and had reached the stage of considering the ground, or where the tenant admitted it. Bahadur Singh v. Muni Subrat Dass, Kaushalya Devi v. K. L. Bansal, and Ferozi Lal v. Man Mal invalidated consent decrees where there was no material showing the tribunal’s satisfaction or the tenant’s acceptance of the statutory ground; they were distinguishable on that basis. The separate opinion also relied on the principle underlying Order 23, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure and on Barton v. Fincham, Thorne v. Smith, Middleton v. Baldock, Babu Ram Sharma v. Pal Singh, and Vas Dev v. Milkhi Ram.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and landlord_asserted_permitted_ground and eviction_order_followed_compromise and (relevant_material_before_consent or tenant_admitted_or_withdrew_ground_defence)

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought proceedings under a rent-control scheme seeking to evict a tenant.
predicates.landlord_asserted_permitted_ground: The landlord sought possession on a ground that the governing law permits as a basis for eviction.
predicates.eviction_order_followed_compromise: The tribunal ordered eviction after the parties reached a compromise or the tenant consented to eviction.
predicates.relevant_material_before_consent: Before the compromise or consent, material supporting the landlord’s asserted ground was before the tribunal at a stage when it could consider that ground.
predicates.tenant_admitted_or_withdrew_ground_defen: The tenant admitted the asserted ground or withdrew the defence to it.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction in rent-control proceedings on a permitted ground and the tribunal has relevant material before a consent order or the tenant admits or withdraws the defence to that ground, the consent eviction decree is enforceable.

issues.legal_issue: An executing court may consider relevant material to decide whether a rent-control eviction decree is a nullity for want of the required statutory basis.
material_facts: The tenant objected to execution on the ground that the eviction decree was a nullity because the tribunal had not independently satisfied itself about the landlord’s bona fide requirement.
The landlord relied on the evidence and documents that had been before the tribunal before the compromise.
The Court rejected the contention that consideration of the nullity objection would require an impermissibly elaborate enquiry.
issues.conclusion: The executing court may adjudicate a plea that an eviction decree is void and consider relevant material to determine whether the tribunal’s required satisfaction existed.
issues.legal_principle: A party may raise before the executing court the objection that a decree is void and therefore inexecutable. In deciding that objection, the executing court may consider relevant material bearing on whether the tribunal had the satisfaction required for an eviction order; the possibility that this requires examining the record does not prevent it from doing so.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party sought to enforce an eviction decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.decree_challenged_as_statutory_nullity: The opposing party claimed that the eviction decree was void because a required statutory basis for eviction was absent.
predicates.relevant_record_material_exists: Material in the record bears on whether the tribunal considered or was satisfied about the asserted ground for eviction.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree is challenged in execution as lacking a required statutory basis and relevant record material exists, the executing court may assess that material.

issues.legal_issue: Defences that a tenant unconditionally withdraws in the eviction proceedings do not remain for reconsideration on a request to remand the matter.
material_facts: The tenant had raised objections concerning the landlord’s title and the validity of the notice terminating the tenancy.
The tenant unconditionally withdrew all defences and submitted to an eviction decree.
The tenant later sought a remand so that those objections could be considered.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused a remand because the tenant had unconditionally withdrawn those defences, which no longer survived for consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Where a tenant unconditionally withdraws all defences in the eviction proceedings, those withdrawn objections do not remain for later adjudication merely because the tenant raises them again in opposing execution or seeks a remand.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought proceedings under a rent-control scheme seeking to evict a tenant.
predicates.tenant_unconditionally_withdrew_defences: The tenant unconditionally withdrew the defences previously raised in the eviction proceedings.
predicates.tenant_later_sought_reconsideration: The tenant later asked for withdrawn objections to be considered or for the matter to be remanded for that purpose.

issues.definition: If a tenant unconditionally withdraws defences in rent-control eviction proceedings and later seeks their reconsideration, those defences are not open for reconsideration.
